text:
maria.g: FYI escalating — we're getting 5 customers in the last 10m reporting sudden 429s after the rate-policy cutover in eu-west-1. customer pings show 429 + "quota_exhausted". Request IDs: req=0a1b2c3d, req=9f8e7d6c. Can we triage?

ajay: Seen the alerts. Is this the scheduled canary from this morning? Which policy variant rolled? :eyes: 

maria.g: Yes, canary pushed at 08:12UTC. Policy name `rl-v2-burst10`. It replaced rl-v1 for ~2% of traffic. Canary config snippet we used: ```json
{"policy":"rl-v2-burst10","burst_window_ms":2000,"rate_per_min":60000,"mode":"enforce"}```

kevin: quick check — are these customers on older billing plans that map to different rate buckets? Billing/quotas mapping runs in a batch job that sometimes hasn't synced with policy changes.

billing-bot: Noted: multiple accounts flagged as `past_due` had limits previously set to legacy-tier. The canary evaluation path used the new policy which expects mapped tiers. Mismatch -> enforced at new, lower allowed tokens.

ajay: Can you paste a representative error payload from the API logs? Need headers + rate-limit response.

maria.g: Pasting sanitized payload: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d
content-type: application/json
retry-after: 30
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "details": "applied_policy=rl-v2-burst10, effective_limit=120/min, observed=240/min"
}```

kevin: That `observed` > `effective_limit` makes sense if customers had active long-running streams. rl-v2 lowered per-min but tightened burst window.

support-ops: Is this reproducing in staging with synthetic traffic? We can repro if we replay recorded traffic from those accounts.

ajay: I'll try a replay against the canary pool. Quick repro steps: 1) set client headers to include legacy-plan header `X-Cust-Tier: legacy` 2) stream 3 concurrent sessions with 1 req/s each for 2 minutes. Should trigger the sawtooth 429 pattern.

sre-bot: Alert: spike in 429 rate (eu-west-1) - +420% over baseline. Canary deployment `rl-v2-burst10` -> 2% traffic.

maria.g: Customers are unhappy — some opened tickets with screenshots. Support thread IDs: T-5532, T-5537.

kevin: Recommended immediate mitigation options: 1) flip policy back to `rl-v1` for the canary cohort (rollback), 2) or set `rl-v2` into `shadow` mode so enforcement stops and only logs hits, 3) increase burst_window_ms to 5000 temporarily. Which do we want?

ajay: Order of ops: shadow -> run replay for 5m -> if stable then re-evaluate config -> or rollback if we need to restore customer traffic immediately. Shadowing is lower-risk.

support-ops: For customers on past_due, we should still be careful — billing-bot indicates those accounts should keep legacy limits until mapping finishes. Can we whitelist the affected account IDs temporarily?

billing-bot: We can add temporary exemptions. List needed. We'll also create a billing ticket to sync tier mappings and apply credits for impacted periods.

maria.g: I'll DM the list of 5 impacted org IDs to @billing-bot now.

kevin: CLI rollback snippet if needed: ```bash
redwoodctl policies set --cohort canary --policy rl-v1 --confirm
```

ajay: Shadow mode toggle: ```bash
redwoodctl policies update rl-v2-burst10 --mode shadow --cohort canary
```

maria.g: Action plan agreed: 1) ajay -> toggle rl-v2 to shadow for canary (now) 2) kevin -> prepare rollback command in case shadow doesn't stabilize within 7m 3) billing-bot -> whitelist 5 orgs and open billing sync ticket 4) support-ops -> notify affected customers with temp workaround and ETA 5) postmortem owner: maria.g

ajay: Toggling to shadow now. Will post back with status.

sre-bot: Policy `rl-v2-burst10` mode changed to `shadow` for cohort `canary` by ajay at 08:23:12 UTC.

maria.g: After switching to shadow, customers reporting immediate relief — 2 of 5 confirmed traffic resumed. :thumbsup:

kevin: Good. Still want to capture replay data + histogram of inter-request intervals to understand why sawtooth hits occur. Suggest we preserve 10m of raw request logs for the impacted orgs.

support-ops: Communicated to customers: "We've temporarily disabled enforcement for your traffic while we investigate. We're collecting logs and will apply credits for any degraded requests."

billing-bot: Whitelist applied for IDs [org_112, org_334, org_778, org_992, org_555]. Billing ticket created: BT-9876.

maria.g: Moving to postmortem docs. Immediate followups: - add a step to the rollout playbook to verify billing-tier mappings before canary enforces, - add automated preflight that runs a sample mapping check for cohorts, - default new policies to `shadow` for the first 30m unless explicitly opted-in.

kevin: I'll draft the playbook changes. Also suggest we add a dashboard tile for canary-enforced rate mismatch alerts.

ajay: Closing loop here: shadow mode held for 12m with no new 429 escalations. Will keep the canary paused and run a controlled replay tomorrow after patches.

maria.g: Thanks all. I'll open the postmortem and link tickets. If anyone sees regressions ping me. :pray:
